title: QPS and Throughput Estimation
description: Learn to calculate queries per second (QPS) and throughput requirements to size servers and infrastructure correctly.

data.text: **Queries Per Second (QPS)** measures how many requests a system must handle each second. Estimating QPS is the first step in capacity planning because it directly determines how many servers, load balancers, and database replicas you need.

Start with daily active users (DAU) and their average requests per day. Divide by the number of seconds in a day (86,400) to get peak QPS. A common rule of thumb is that peak traffic is about 2–3 times the average.

rows: Average requests per user per day

data.title: Rule of Thumb
data.text: Always plan for 3x peak and 5x spike traffic. Interviewers expect you to account for sudden viral moments or marketing campaigns.
Once you have peak QPS, you can estimate server count. A well-tuned web server typically handles 1,000–2,000 QPS. For 17,361 peak QPS, you would need roughly 9–18 web servers behind a load balancer.

Most applications are read-heavy. A typical ratio is 100:1 (reads to writes). For a social media feed, reads dominate because users scroll through hundreds of posts without creating content. Separate your read and write QPS calculations because they require different architectures.

terms.definition: Queries Per Second — the number of requests a system handles each second.
The total amount of data or requests processed over a given period.
The maximum expected request rate, typically 2–3 times the average.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Calculate average QPS from DAU and requests per user
Multiply by 3x for peak and 5x for spikes
Read QPS is often 100x write QPS
Server count = peak QPS divided by capacity per server
data.takeaway: QPS estimation drives every downstream capacity decision.

data.title: Practice Calculation
data.description: Calculate QPS for a music streaming service with 5 million DAU, where each user streams 20 songs and makes 10 API calls per day.

items.question: What if I don't know the DAU?
items.answer: Make reasonable assumptions and state them clearly. Interviewers care more about your methodology than exact numbers.

items.question: Should I include batch jobs in QPS?
items.answer: Separate batch workloads from real-time QPS. Batch jobs run during off-peak hours and have different resource requirements.
